title: TSP Modernization Act of 2017
official_summary:
TSP Modernization Act of 2017

(Sec. 2) This bill modifies the rules relating to withdrawals from the Thrift Savings Plan accounts of former federal employees and Members of Congress. Under current law, such employees and Members may make only one partial withdrawal upon reaching age 59-1/2 while employed or one withdrawal after retirement. The bill permits an unlimited number of such withdrawals.

The bill also eliminates: (1) the automatic annuity as a default option if the plan participant does not make an election to establish an annuity, and (2) the limitation on age-based in-service withdrawals.

summary.headline: A 2017 law changes how federal employees and Members of Congress can take money out of their Thrift Savings Plan accounts.
summary.what_it_does: Before this law, people with Thrift Savings Plan accounts could make only one partial withdrawal after reaching age 59 and a half while still working, or one withdrawal after retiring. The law allows an unlimited number of these withdrawals. It also removes the automatic annuity that applied when a participant did not choose an annuity, and it removes the limit on age-based withdrawals while still employed.

who_it_affects.group: Current and former federal employees with Thrift Savings Plan accounts
who_it_affects.how: They can take more than one withdrawal under the age-based and post-retirement rules instead of only one.

who_it_affects.group: Members of Congress with Thrift Savings Plan accounts
who_it_affects.how: They can take an unlimited number of withdrawals under the same rules instead of only one.

who_it_affects.group: Participants who do not make an annuity election
who_it_affects.how: They no longer receive an automatic annuity as the default outcome if they do not choose one.
